articles.title: RBI Keeps Policy Repo Rate Unchanged at 6.5% for Consecutive Meeting
articles.summary: The RBI Monetary Policy Committee kept the repo rate unchanged while focusing on inflation control and economic growth.
articles.why_it_matters: Monetary policy decisions directly affect banking operations, liquidities, and government bond yields. Questions on policy rates (Repo, Reverse Repo, MSF, Bank Rate) are mandatory segments in IBPS PO, SBI PO, and RBI Grade B general awareness phases.
articles.detailed_explanation: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) decided to keep the policy repo rate unchanged at 6.50% in its latest session. The committee also maintained its policy stance of 'withdrawal of accommodation' to align consumer inflation targets (CPI) progressively with the medium-term goal of 4.0%, while ensuring stable GDP expansion guidelines. Credit reserves remain robust across public lenders.
articles.exam_relevance: Direct questions on repo rate, reverse repo, bank rate, marginal standing facility (MSF), and policy stance occur in almost every IBPS and SBI mains paper.
key_facts: Policy Repo Rate remains at 6.50%
Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate stands at 6.25%
Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) and Bank Rate stand at 6.75%
MPC voted with a 5-to-1 majority
Target CPI inflation rate is maintained at 4.0% with a +/- 2.0% tolerance band
articles.memory_points: Remember: Repo is the rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks. When Repo remains unchanged, interest rates on retail/home loans generally remain stable.
exam_questions: What is the current policy repo rate as of the latest RBI MPC meeting?
Explain the objective behind the RBI's policy stance of 'withdrawal of accommodation'.

articles.detailed_explanation: Global and domestic credit rating agencies have revised India's real GDP growth forecast upward for fiscal year 2026-27 to 7.2%. The upgrades are supported by solid recovery in agricultural sectors, a resurgence in private consumer demand, and sustained government infrastructure capital expenditures.
articles.exam_relevance: Questions asking about the specific GDP growth percentage projected by rating agencies or multilateral banks are standard in current affairs sections.

Capital expenditure growth rate stands at 11% annually
Key drivers: Rural consumption, industrial investments, and service exports resilience

articles.title: Retail Inflation Cools Down to 4.2% Easing Liquidity Stances

This moderation was driven by food and energy price stabilizes, aligning the CPI output close to the RBI's comfort band of 4% (+/- 2%). Easing inflation reduces the pressure on short-term banking liquidity.
articles.exam_relevance: Standard question topic in RBI Grade B and SBI PO mains. Knowledge of WPI vs. CPI index parameters is essential.
